text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- U.S. President Bill Clinton tells Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat: We can't stop Har Homa.
- Top Likud figures, in dig at Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, blast central committee "one-man show".
- February budget deficit lower than expected at 561 million shekels, Finance Ministry says.
- Israeli bank workers demanding five-day work week call off strike planned for Tuesday.
- Africa Israel's new shopping mall in Ramat Aviv near Tel Aviv will close on Jewish sabbaths.
- Israel signs investment deals with nine countries: Uzbekistan, Albania, Ukraine, Argentina, Georgia, India, Turkey, Turkmenistan and Kazakhstan.
- Workers at Israel Chemicals Ltd step up bid for company shares.
- Government to accelerate cuts in labour force.
- Spanish conglomerate Sol-Melia to invest in hotels in Israel.
GLOBES
- Recovery in industrial production, drop in imports and rise in unemployment in December-January.
HAARETZ
- Clinton raises the level of relations with the Palestinian Authority, criticises building on Har Homa. Netanyahu denies delay on survey work connected to his Egypt trip on Wednesday.
- French foreign minister in Israel: "Without a doubt, Syria is looking for a peace agreement."
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Clinton-Arafat front against building on Har Homa.
- Hamas suspect accused of murdering with axes, torturing with chains, shredding with knives.
MAARIV

- Communications Ministry in High Court challenge against decision that Bezeq Communications director-designate Yoram Turbowicz must wait a year before taking job. He was head of government Antitrust Authority until Bezeq appointment on Sunday.
